expected_behavior: Calls list_monitors first to check the URL is not already monitored, because create_monitor is not idempotent
Confirms the exact URL with the user before creating
Calls create_monitor with the url
If the user also wanted authentication or custom headers, creates the monitor and tells them to add those in the dashboard rather than claiming the MCP can set them

query: I just deployed the billing service. What should I monitor?
expected_behavior: Calls list_monitors to assess current coverage before recommending anything
Recommends the specific gaps (new endpoints or health checks with no monitor) and waits for confirmation instead of creating monitors silently
On confirmation, calls create_monitor for each approved URL
Where a new monitor sits behind an already-monitored upstream, offers register_monitor_dependency so the downstream check does not page when the upstream is down
Picks the matching type for each gap (tcp for a database port, heartbeat for a scheduled job) and defers only what needs credentials (ssh, sftp, logins) to the dashboard

query: I'm adding a nightly database backup cron job. Make sure we hear about it if it stops running.
expected_behavior: Calls create_monitor with type=heartbeat, a name and intervalSeconds matching the schedule (86400 for nightly), after confirming the schedule
Does not invent a ping URL: explains that the tool does not return it and that the user copies it from the monitor's page in the dashboard
Writes the job's ping call so it reads the URL from an environment variable or secret store, not hard-coded or committed
Does not ask the user to paste the ping URL into the chat
Mentions that checking starts after the first ping

query: Monitor our Postgres on db.example.com and the SSH port on bastion.example.com.
expected_behavior: Calls create_monitor with type=tcp, url=db.example.com and port=5432 for the database
Does not try to create an ssh monitor over MCP; explains it needs credentials and is set up in the dashboard (or offers a tcp check on port 22 for plain reachability)
Confirms both targets with the user before creating
Calls get_overview first — one call answers the question and groups monitors that failed the same way at the same target into a single outage instead of one row each
Reports the distinct outages rather than a raw monitor count, so forty symptoms of one failure are not read as forty incidents
For a specific monitor, calls list_status_changes and then get_root_cause with a statusChangeId for per-probe diagnostics
Falls back to list_monitors with status=[down] only when the raw per-monitor inventory is genuinely needed
Summarizes what is down without calling any write tool for this read-only question

query: We're deploying tonight from 22:00 to 23:00 — don't page us.
expected_behavior: Identifies the affected monitors via list_monitors
Resolves the 22:00-23:00 window's timezone (passes an IANA timezone or converts to UTC) and confirms it with the user before writing
Calls create_maintenance with monitorIds, scheduleType=once, startTime, durationMinutes and timezone so alerts are suppressed during the window
Confirms the window is in place via list_maintenance (status=active or upcoming)
Finds the staging monitor via list_monitors
Confirms before pausing, noting that a real outage will not page while the monitor is paused
Calls pause_monitor with the monitor id
Mentions resume_monitor to restart it later rather than treating the pause as permanent

query: Check the staging monitor every 5 minutes instead of every minute.
expected_behavior: Finds the staging monitor via list_monitors to get its id
Calls update_monitor with the id and intervalSeconds=300 (5 minutes), leaving the name unchanged

Does not recreate the monitor and does not claim it can change the URL, type, auth, or thresholds via MCP — only name and check interval are editable through update_monitor, the rest stays in the dashboard
Confirms the new interval rather than treating the other settings as changed

query: Open an incident for the API outage.
expected_behavior: Calls create_incident with title, impact, message and affectedMonitorIds
Tells the user the incident is an unpublished draft (not public, subscribers not notified) that they publish from the dashboard
Does not claim it has published the incident or notified subscribers
Optionally uses post_incident_update as the situation develops and resolve_incident when it is over

query: Add monitors for our 60 endpoints. Which plan do we need for that, and how much will it cost?
expected_behavior: Calls get_plan to read the current plan, its monitor limit and its price before creating anything
Calls list_plans and compares the included monitors, extraMonitorMonthly and the monthly and annual prices of the plans that fit 60 monitors
Quotes prices exactly as returned (VAT is included where it applies, sales tax is added at checkout) and does not invent a plan, price or limit
Says that the plan is changed in the dashboard, not through the MCP server, and does not start creating monitors past the current limit without the user's go-ahead
